Well, no, I mean... I wasn't really stressed when this started. I actually came in to see you because... well, I just can't shake this feeling I have at work. Leaving their wrappers and pencils everywhere. I swear I buy a new box of those yellow Ticonderoga pencils every month. Gary's wife just had a baby, a little girl, so I suppose he's sleep-deprived. I remember when my daughter was born, I didn't sleep a full night for almost a year. I'll say, \"What was that?\" or \"Excuse me?\" and then I look around and... I'm completely alone. It's very strange. But then I'll just go back to grading. I'll just be sitting there, and I'll hear this woman's voice say my name, or make a short comment about what I'm doing, like \"look at that.\" It's so clear that I actually answer her out loud before I realize there's absolutely no one else in the room. \n\nWhich is a bit like my cat, Barnaby. Everything is plastic now. I try to use reusable containers to be good to the environment, but it's just so much washing up at the end of the day. My dishwasher has been making this awful grinding noise lately, too. I think a piece of glass might be stuck in the drain from when I broke a wine glass last month. Like last Tuesday, I was just sitting quietly at my desk during my planning period.
